# Contract terms

Summary of the Tern-9 refit contract (HRA-T9-2190-07, with Ostrander Orbital) and the Pellam Systems firmware supply agreement (PS-SA-2190-22) as they bear on the Echo Case. Prepared by Case Command for the Director. Commercial figures are rounded.

## Tern-9 refit contract

| Clause | Term |
|---|---|
| Scope | Refit of Tern-9: dish array rebuild, shielding, transmit power train, shielded bunks, cable runs |
| Price | 412 M credits, fixed, plus change orders |
| Schedule | Station access from 27 Jan 2191 (held to 31 Jan 2192); refit complete (M5) 15 Dec 2191 |
| Liquidated damages | 0.4 M credits per day late after 15 Dec, capped at 30 M |
| Product risk | Defective supplied firmware or boards are replaced under the vendor's warranty; the schedule loss is the Authority's, and the contractor keeps working |
| Design risk | A finding of **design risk** (a signal or behaviour outside the agreed basis) suspends the contractor's open work orders pending an Authority design review; the contractor is paid standby at 40 % |
| Schedule bonus | 18 M credits to Ostrander if M5 is met on 15 Dec 2191 |
| Station stock | Panels on the dish remain Authority property; the contractor may not replace a panel without a purchase order (panel 7 has none) |

## Pellam Systems supply agreement

| Clause | Term |
|---|---|
| Product | Relay receive-timing firmware, builds 5–9, and receiver boards flashed with them |
| Warranty | Conformance to specification PS-S7 at delivery |
| Band | Specification PS-S7 covers the timing path for the 1.4–2.0 GHz traffic band; behaviour of the analogue front end outside that band is the buyer's design risk |
| Remedy | Rebuild and reflash of non-conforming builds at Pellam's cost |

## Why this matters

If the echo is a *firmware* defect, Pellam reflashes forty relays, the contractor keeps working, Ostrander keeps its 18 M bonus, and the Ministry is told about a patch. If the echo is a *design* matter (a signal outside the agreed basis), the refit stops, the contractor sits on 40 % standby for however long the review takes, the bonus is gone, and the Ministry will ask what signal.

So a bad-build story suits two parties: the contractor, which keeps its schedule and its bonus, and a Director who wants the Net trusted until she understands what is answering it. That is why Corin Ashdale wrote to Pellam, and why the Director asked him to. See [[Intercepted message]].
